newsitem.title: USA: BPA bid to lift intertie usage clears first hurdle.
newsitem.headline: BPA bid to lift intertie usage clears first hurdle.

text.p: A plan to raise capacity limits on Pacific Intertie power lines by almost 25 percent was approved by a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) study group late Friday, a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) spokeswoman said over the weekend.
The federal power marketing agency, which owns and operates the Northwest portion of the intertie, hopes to raise capacity limits by March, said spokeswoman Cheri Larson.
BPA has sought to raise combined capacity of the lines to 6,500 megawatts (MW) from 5,200 MW, and the group has approved a limit of 6,250 MW, she said.
Operation of the lines was cut to 65 percent capacity in August after two major power outages hit the West last summer.
The WSCC study group now has until the end of the week to make some minor revisions to the BPA proposal.
On Friday, the plan will be forwarded to the WSCC's board of trustees, which has an additional 10 days to make a final decision.
BPA also plans to install new equipment to allow capacity to rise in stages to full rates in time for the April runoff, when hydroelectric dam output increases.
The AC segment of the intertie has a rated capacity 4,800 megawatts (MW), compared with a current limit of 3,200 MW. The DC line is rated at 3,200 MW, but was limited to 2,000 MW.
